_comment: Model manifest. Every URL and sizeBytes here was verified against the Hugging Face Hub
and the GitHub releases they come from, not copied from a README.
Digests: the VAD and ASR entries carry SHA-256 values computed by downloading those exact
URLs and hashing the bytes. The GGUF chat models do not, because their digests are not
retrievable without downloading several gigabytes each. Their sizeBytes are exact, which
is what catches the realistic failure (a truncated or interrupted download); a substituted
file would not be caught, and hashVerified:false says so. The installer treats a null
digest as size-checked only and the UI tells the user.
Tier mapping is deliberate. An 8 GB phone is offered a small chat model and no heavy one;
12 GB gets Phi-4-mini for chat and Qwen3-4B as the heavy tier; 16 GB+ gets Qwen3-8B.
requiredFreeMb is roughly the file plus KV cache and runtime overhead, so the selector
refuses a model that would be OOM-killed next to the ASR pipeline.

models.notes: Gates ASR so speech recognition only runs on actual speech. Tiny, and the single biggest battery saving in the pipeline. Without it the app falls back to an energy threshold.
English transcription. Archive contains encoder.int8.onnx, decoder.int8.onnx, joiner.int8.onnx and tokens.txt; the installer flattens them into models/asr/ and discards the bundled test audio.
The smallest chat model that is still useful. Fits an 8 GB phone alongside the recorder. Note this one is under Google's Gemma terms, not a standard open licence.
Preferred chat model on an 8 GB phone: noticeably better than the 1B while still leaving room for the recorder.
The always-ready assistant on a 12 GB phone. Loaded on demand and unloaded a few minutes later, so it is not resident all day.
Heavy tier for a 12 GB phone, run only while charging and idle. Whether the 8B fits here instead is a question for the on-device benchmark, not a guess.
Heavy tier for 16 GB and larger phones. Five gigabytes of weights, so charging and idle only.
